utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Salihamidzic. Yesterday you were telling the Trial Chamber about a conversation on the 9th of September, 1993 with Mr. Edib Saric and your chief, Mr. Emin Zebic.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'd just take you back one -- one moment to remind you of what you said yesterday. You said that Mr. Edib Saric had confirmed that you insisted in view of the fact that he had -- that army troops were insisted -- that you insisted some of the military go with you to Grabovica. Now, who was Mr. Edib Saric?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know Edib Saric before that, but I was told that he was the commander of a unit called Igman Wolves, which was billeted on the left bank of the Neretva River in Grabovica on the premises of the administration of the Grabovica hydroelectric power plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And we know it's been a long time, but could you, if possible, just tell the Trial Chamber what the information was that you were given at that point about civilians being killed. Just -- just try and be as specific as you can.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They still didn't have any reliable information other than they assumed that there were some civilians who were killed in the village of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your information at that point as to who had killed the civilians?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Edib Saric himself said that units had arrived from Sarajevo and that it was most likely that soldiers from those units who arrived from Sarajevo did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did Mr. Zebic instruct you to do?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic told me that it would be good to go to Grabovica to check the information. I then suggested, since these were military formations, to also take somebody from the unit, from the military structures. So we agreed to ask that the commander of the military police unit comes with us, which Zebic agreed to. So within the hour, as soon as we found him, Sead Kurt and I - who is the military police commander in the 44th Brigade - set off in a military -- in a police vehicle, which I drove to Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Was Grabovica within your police station's area of responsibility or jurisdiction?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Our police station was next to the Aleksin Han bridge in the direction of Mostar. Grabovica is about 5 kilometres farther down-river from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it within the jurisdiction of the Mostar police?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know of any reason why the Mostar police couldn't have gone to Grabovica on that day or weren't involved in this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first part of the question is not objectable -- objectionable. The witness hasn't given any evidence at all as to the second part of it. So the question itself has got two parts. The first part, I don't object to. The second part, I would. And in any event, putting the two questions in one question can't be right. So that's the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe the answer to the first question is very simple. Then Mr. Re asked the second question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But if there's an objection, Mr. Re, maybe you split your question. Ask this witness one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm actually only trying to speed things up, but that's why I asked the two at once on something I didn't think was an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, do you know of any reason why the Mostar police couldn't have gone to Grabovica on that day? As briefly as possible.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main road to Mostar was blocked. It was exposed to the fire of the HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What time did you get to Grabovica approximately?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived at Grabovica at 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far -- or where did you go to in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived on the inhabited part on the right bank of the Neretva River. That was the village of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came to the village, in front of the building where the old railway station used to be there was an improvised checkpoint that was set up and a soldier was standing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did the soldier do?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped the car. We came out, showed our ID. He asked us where we were going. I said that we were there to speak to some of the commanders. He told us that about 10 metres from the place where we were talking -- and he showed us one of two men in civilian clothing who were there, and he said that that was his commander. We went inside. This man approached us. That was the commander of the Independent Battalion. He introduced himself. Next to him was another man, also in civilian clothes. He was a refugee. His name was Zulfo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did the -- what was the name of the commander of the Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know -- I didn't find that out immediately, but later I found out that it was Adnan Solakovic. He did introduce himself, but I didn't really understand it or hear it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know a person called Ivan Pranjic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Stoja Pranjic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stoja Pranjic is the wife of Ivan Pranjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see them when you went to Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We first spoke with Adnan and Zulfo, and then later in the courtyard of the house I saw Ivan and Stoja Pranjic. They were very frightened. I talked to them for a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Let's just go back to your conversation with Adnan Solakovic. What did he tell you? What did you speak about?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to Adnan Solakovic, and he told me that over the past 24 hours at least five civilians were killed of Croat ethnicity. He -- this refugee who had been there for some time told me their names. The refugee's name, again, was Zulfo. I found out that they were most probably killed and the people who were most probably killed were Marinko Maric, his wife Luca, his father Martin, their neighbour Ilka Maric, and her daughter, Ruzica. Yes, Ruzica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Zulfo tell you about how they had been killed or what had happened to them?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo said, and Adnan confirmed it, that soldiers of the unit which was about 100 metres down-river towards Mostar had killed those civilians. Zulfo said the same thing. According to what they said, the three women's bodies were seen near the house of Marinko Maric and the body of Maric Marinko was up-river from this checkpoint, at which point we entered, towards a place called Crno Vrelo. That was perhaps some 300 metres up-river. The body of Marinko Maric was lying below the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Salihamidzic, know any of the people you just listed as having been probably killed on that day: Marinko Maric, Luca Maric, Martin Maric, Ilka Maric, and Ruzica Maric?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I personally knew Marinko Maric. I met him in 1992 when I worked in UNIS in Jablanica and he worked in Igman. Those two companies had a business arrangement, and that's when we met. At the same time, I met his wife Luca. He was a mechanical engineer by profession.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was the name of the unit to which the soldiers belonged that Adnan Solakovic said had killed the civilians?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the unit was called, but I know who the commander of the unit was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Adnan told me that on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That what was done -- actually, that the soldiers were killed by soldiers of the unit that was billeted downriver, and the commander was -- of that unit was Ramiz Delalic, Celo. Can I add something? Adnan also told me that we should not be going down to the other checkpoint, because he would not be able to guarantee that we would come back alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you see the other checkpoint from where you were near the old railway station?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could. It was about 100 metres down-river before the road that turns right into the village. From before, I know that the house of Anto Maric was behind the checkpoint, and there was a soldier standing at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know what Adnan Solakovic's soldiers were doing when the civilians were being killed?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than the soldier at the first checkpoint, I didn't see any other soldiers. I don't know what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Adnan Solakovic tell you where he was or what his soldiers were doing at the time when the civilians, the five civilians you named earlier, were killed by soldiers of the other unit?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't say anything. He didn't tell me. The only thing he told me was that he couldn't guarantee that Ivan and Stoja would stay alive. Actually, he said the following: That they shouldn't try anything with Celo's unit; otherwise, these people would not stay alive. And he said that we should try to get those two elderly people out of there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you when you spoke to him about whether or not he was in a position to prevent any killings in the village?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He just said that only through a fight between his unit and the unit of Ramiz Delalic, Celo, could this killing have been prevented.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You spoke earlier about Ivan and Stoja Pranjic. You said they were in the courtyard. Were they there with -- were they participating in the conversation between you and Mr. Solakovic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very little, because they were very frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you known them from before?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was better acquainted with Ivan. I only knew Stoja by sight. Earlier I used to go fishing in that area, so I knew Ivan very well. Also, they were the mother and father of a neighbour of mine in Jablanica. Her name is Krstic Olga.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were Ivan and Stoja Pranjic residents of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they permanently resided in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said that Adnan Solakovic expressed some concern for their safety. What was your response?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him that I would try to do that, because I knew their son-in-law, Nehru Manjusak, and I said that I would tell him. He was a cook in Zulfikar Alispago's unit, and I intended to go and see him immediately to tell him that he should try to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've said you saw -- there was a soldier at the checkpoint when you came into the village. You spoke to Mr. Solakovic. You saw another -- another soldier at another checkpoint about 100 metres away. At that particular point, when you were talking to Mr. Solakovic, did you -- were there any other soldiers in the area?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for the soldier at the checkpoint, there were no other soldiers. I didn't see any, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear anything that indicated that soldiers were in the area?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could hear several shots fired in the depth of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were they coming from, these shots?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the road in the direction of the railway tracks, deeper inside the village, on the right bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A little earlier you said that Zulfo had said that three women's bodies were near the house of Marinko Maric and Maric Maric [sic] was up-river from the checkpoint and the body of Marinko Maric was lying below the road. Did --

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- he say anything about Martin Maric, where his body was?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody knew about Martin Maric's body. He was paralysed. He lay in his house. I know that Marinko's wife, Luca, took care of him. She even came from Konjic and left her husband there in order to care for his father.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: After speaking to Mr. Solakovic in the old railway station, what did you and Kurt do?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After finding out the information, we started back. And then we agreed to go in the direction of Crno Vrelo, in the direction of Jablanica, and that he would look on the right side of the road and I would look at the left side of the road. After covering about 150 to 200 metres, we stopped at a shoulder of the road. This was at my suggestion because already you couldn't see down to the Neretva from the right side of the road. So I parked the car. He stayed by the car. And we had a look around. I went all the way down to the river bed to check if perhaps the body that they were talking about hadn't been pushed into the river. But I didn't see anything. I didn't find the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just going back very briefly. You -- you said you spoke to Mr. Solakovic. Then you started back. When you came out of the railway station speaking to Mr. Solakovic, was the soldier who had stopped you at first still there?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the soldier was there. He came up to me and said that he was afraid that the soldiers in the unit next to them were committing killings, and he was afraid because he wasn't a Muslim. I went back briefly and told Adnan what he said and told him that it would be good if he moved him from there so that -- to prevent anything from happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did he say the soldiers were killing?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were killing the Croat inhabitants of Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you drive back along the side of the road looking -- what were you looking for when you drove back towards Jablanica with Mr. Kurt?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wanted to check if Marinko Maric's body was still there, which was mentioned during our conversation with Zulfo. Zulfo said that the body was after the checkpoint towards the Crno Jezero [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that all you were looking for, just his body specifically, or were you looking for other things along the way?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His body or anything else. Anything that would confirm what they had told us. Regardless of the body that we found, we would look and stop and inspect the body; However, we didn't find any body -- any bodies.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It's not Crno Jezero but Crno Vrelo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you were down by the river looking for the body, was there any traffic on the road?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I had looked around on my way back, I noticed that across the bridge at Crno Vrelo in the direction of Jablanica a car passed. I asked Kurt, "Who was it that passed?" And he said that Celo had come by in his car, had stopped next to him, and asked him, "Are you looking?" And -- but, "Just look at what they're doing to our people." And he was probably thinking of the refugees, the people who had been brought from the Dretelj camp and who were accommodated in the settlement on the left bank in Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Where did you go with Mr. Kurt after that?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went back to Jablanica to convey all the information to our superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Approximately how long was it between when you left and when you returned to the police station? I mean, what time did you get back approximately?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't really paying attention to that, but perhaps the whole thing lasted from an hour to an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Ivan and Stoja Pranjic? Did they go back with you?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They remained there. Upon returning to Jablanica, I immediately went to the police station. My chief, Emin Zebic, was there. I informed him orally about what I had found out. And immediately afterwards, I went to Olga Krstic's house. I found her brother-in-law, Nehru, there and told him that he should go there and save Ivan and Stoja, to save Ivan and Stoja. He said that he'd ask Zuka to go down there together and to do that. And that's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why didn't you and Mr. Kurt take Ivan and Stoja Pranjic back with you?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were a little afraid because of the warning Adnan Solakovic had given us. We were afraid that we might be intercepted on the way, on the right bank by these soldiers and that because we were taking them away, they might attack us, as well as these Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What's your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim, a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just said that you orally informed Mr. Zebic about what -- what you'd found out. Did he give you any instructions about what you should do?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact I made a suggestion; I suggested that we wait, because it was necessary to get Ivan and Stoja out rapidly, and I said it would be good to wait to see whether they would come and then to gather more information and that afterwards I would draft the written part of the report, and he agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, moving to the next day, which was September the 10th. Did you see the Pranjics on the 10th?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning, on the 10th, perhaps at about 9.00 or half past 9.00, between 9.00 and 10.00, I went to Olga Krstic's house. That's their -- she's their daughter. And I saw Ivan and Stoja there. I spoke to them. Ivan was a fairly taciturn man. Stoja would speak the most. I asked them to tell me the first and last names and the approximate age of all the Croat inhabitants who lived on the right bank at the time. She did that, and I compiled the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many were on the list?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 30 individuals on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it a handwritten list you compiled?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to your list? Or what did you do with it?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, I had other things to do. I had to gather other information. So on the following day, I drafted an official note. That was on the 11th. And the list was attached to that note.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How had Ivan and Stoja Pranjic managed to get from Grabovica to Jablanica by the 10th of September?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told me that their son-in-law -- their daughter's son-in-law had appeared with Zuka, with Zulfikar Alispago. They arrived in a van and they took them to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you speak to them more - that's Stoja and Ivan Pranjic - about what they had seen or heard in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They'd calmed down a bit. By that time, it was possible to speak to them, and it was Stoja, rather than Ivan, who told me what had happened, who said that on the 8th in the afternoon they were in front of their house. Ivan and Stoja were in front of their house and Marinko Maric appeared and they had a chat. Then the soldiers arrived. They passed by them. And immediately afterwards, shooting broke out, and shortly after that his wife, Luca -- Marinko's wife, Luca, arrived in a state and asked what he was doing there since the troops were driving them out of their houses. And Marinko immediately went downstream with her, because that's where their house was, and Ivan and Stoja didn't see them after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had they seen any bodies?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivan and Stoja hadn't seen any bodies. They didn't dare leave their house. But as these refugees provided them with information on that morning, on the 9th, the refugees from Stolac went to get bread on the left bank of the Neretva and they then noticed a body and they assumed that it could have been Marinko Maric. And some women who had come from Marinko Maric's house said that they had seen three bodies next to Marinko's house, Maric Luca's house, Ilka's -- the bodies of Marinko, Luca, Ilka, and Ruzica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, what about the bridge? Had any of them been on the bridge?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The refugees who went to get bread said that at the bridge that joins the left and right bank they saw blood. They saw blood on the bridge, but there was no body there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was speaking to -- was your speaking to Ivan and Stoja a part of your information-gathering on the 10th of September?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I spoke to them to gather as much information as possible in relation to this affair.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What else did you do on the 10th of September to gather information?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Semso Halebic came to the police station, and I provided him with this information that I had. He was a security officer in the 44th Brigade. I provided him with the information I'd gathered, and he suggested that we speak to some of the guards who were securing the administrative building of the Grabovica hydroelectric power plant. We went there, and we found Alija Turkic, who was on guard duty between the 8th and 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was Alija Turkic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Turkic was an employee of the hydroelectric power plant on the Neretva, a driver by profession. But during this period of time, he worked as a guard in that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were there soldiers at the Grabovica hydroelectric plant? Were there soldiers based there?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the administrative building of the power plant, and the Igman Wolves was located there, which was commanded by Edib Saric.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Alija Turkic tell you?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Turkic more or less confirmed the arrival of the troops in the afternoon on the 8th. He said that as soon as they had arrived on the scene, they started shooting. Then when night started to fall, they lit a fire, and given the noise they were making, he assumed that they had been drinking. So throughout the night between the 8th and the 9th, there was shooting on the right bank. The administrative building is on the left bank of the Neretva. He also said that in the morning at about 5.00, between 5.00 and 6.00, an elderly Croatian married couple came to see him and told him that two elderly Croats had been taken away from their house on the left bank, and they suggested that the command be informed of the fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you mean on that very morning, the morning of the 10th of September? Is that the morning you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, on the 9th of September in the morning. They were there between the 8th and the 9th. It was on the 9th in the morning at about half past 5.00. That's when this elderly couple came to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, did that complete your information-gathering for the day, when you spoke to Mr. Turkic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I thought I had completed my information-gathering, but about 1830 hours Zuka arrived at the station and Edib Saric arrived too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you speak to them?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I spoke to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was Mr. Zebic there when you spoke to them?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zebic was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, what did Zuka and Edib Saric tell you?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They told us that they had surveyed the area and that they had established that on the right bank six bodies had been found and on the left bank two bodies had been found and that among the bodies that had been found on the right bank, there was a child, and apparently 14 inhabitants had been evacuated. And two children were still alive. They had been evacuated too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To -- you mean also? They had also been evacuated? I'm sorry, I heard the word "to" in my hear phones and I thought it was "too," "o-o," the other way around. Mr. Salihamidzic, you were of course just then referring to Grabovica, weren't you, where Zuka and Edib Saric --

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said two children had also been evacuated. In addition to the 14 adults, there were two children who had also been evacuated and they had been put up in Zulfikar Alispago's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you were saying that they had established on the right bank six bodies had been found and on the left bank two bodies had been found, I take it you were referring to the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm referring to the same area that we more or less visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had Zuka and Edib Saric seen or found the bodies themselves, or was it something they had been told?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this was done. They just relayed this information to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the dead child and the two children that were evacuated, were they from the same family?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't know that. Later it was established that they were from that family, Zadro. In fact, Zuka and Edib didn't mention any names. No one mentioned any first or last names. Reference was only made to individuals of Croat nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long was Zuka and Mr. Saric at the police station for?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for very long. They weren't there for very long. Perhaps about 15 minutes. Half an hour at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you communicate with Zuka again that night?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I saw Sejo Brankovic. He was from Mostar. He worked in the Mostar MUP. And at that time, I think he also worked for the State Security Service and he had been deployed in Jablanica. He was in Jablanica. He told me there were problems in Grabovica again and that some girl called (redacted), a girl who worked as a cleaning lady in the settlement up there. She was a refugee, he said, and two other girls had fled and they had fled to the dam of the power plant near Grabovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked whether you had communicated with Zuka again that night, and you said later you saw Sejo Brankovic. How did you come to see Sejo Brankovic and where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. First I met Sejo Brankovic and he told me -- he'd spoken to Zuka over the phone, and he said that we should go to his flat together. That flat was just behind the MUP building, perhaps 50 metres behind it. And we went there together to examine the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's Zuka's flat? You went to Zuka's flat?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we went to Zuka's flat. Zuka was there, Edib Saric was there, and someone called Namik was there. It was said that he worked as a security officer in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember his family name at the moment, Namik?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I found out that his name was Namik Dzankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just to go back slightly. Was it at -- when those people were there that Sejo Brankovic told you about someone having been raped in -- in Grabovica? Was it at that point?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sejo told me that he had such information and this is why we should go to see Zuka. When we arrived in Zuka's flat, Zuka confirmed that certain things had taken place and he in fact confirmed what Sejo Brankovic had previously told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You'd been to Grabovica the day before and Adnan Solakovic had told you about the behaviour of one unit there, which was Celo's unit, which had been killing some Croat civilians. Was that discussed when you were at Zuka's flat?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that was really discussed, but it was said that it was the soldiers who did what they did the previous day, who had raped the girl, the soldiers from the same unit who had killed people moved over to the left bank and raped this refugee girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was any action suggested that should be taken?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what was being discussed when this discussion was interrupted quite abruptly, because Ramiz Delalic, Celo, appeared at the door together with one of his men, who was a large man, just like him. I don't know whether that was his deputy, an escort. And as soon as he entered, he looked in my direction. He looked at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll just stop you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could go into private session for a moment here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- what did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Wait. Wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, before anything happens further, that last part there, in my submission, ought not to be in -- in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll repeat it on record. It's all right. I'll just read the question back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's not necessary. Maybe at a later stage we could have the protective measures lifted later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: With respect to that, yes, Your Honour. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, you were just saying -- I won't go through the whole thing. You were just saying that it had been said that Vehbija Karic had said -- one of the soldiers had asked, "What would happen if one of the Croats were put -- were to put them up, protested?" He said, "Kill them and throw them into the lake, or into the Neretva," or something like that. My question is: When that was said, who was present in the room?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present, Zuka, Edib Saric, Namik, and Sejo Brankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Zuka make a telephone call?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After Celo left the room with his escort, Zuka picked up the receiver, dialed a number, and said that there were problems, that he needed to go back. And then when he hung up, he said, "Sefer is in Konjic" and that he had telephoned him and told him that he should return in order to deal with the problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is Sefer? Who is the Sefer he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When he spoke to the person on the phone, did he use the word "Sefer," or was it something he said afterwards?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less he said, "Sefer, we have problems. You need to come back to Jablanica as soon as possible in order to resolve these problems."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Zebic had asked you to prepare a written report after you'd given him the oral report. Did you prepare a written report? And if so, when?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I made my report the next day, on the 11th, typed it out, and submitted it to Mr. Emin Zebic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown MFI D222.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just have a look at that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown both -- all the pages in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, the -- what's on the English-speaking page seems to be the Brankovic report. I think the -- the English version of this witness's report is on the third page. I just want to be clear. I'm not sure which one my friend wants him to look at, which -- either one he can, of course, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've got the Bosnian on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. The English version on the screen. Now we have the official note here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Yes, that's okay. We have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, can you just -- have you just seen the document? And can you identify that? Is that the official note you prepared in relation to the events in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And is everything recorded in that document based upon the information you gathered, the interviews you had with people, and the conversations you -- you had with the people you've described in your evidence this morning?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is it a compilation of what you knew as of -- about the 11th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'd just like to, if possible, fill in some blanks which appear to be on that particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could just move back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And can you please highlight the first -- or the first half of the page, enlargen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's a name in handwriting at the bottom of the first paragraph to the right --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop. Stop. Stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To the right of the word "batoljona." What's the word there in handwriting?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it now. Could you please scroll it down a little bit more. Just scroll it down a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Up. Up. Up. Stop. Bang in the middle of that one, to the left. This doesn't work very well.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Solakovic. "Solakovic" was written later -- written in later because we found that out later. This is something -- this last name was added in by Mr. Zebic. Although, it's not correct here. It still states "Sokolovic," but it should be Solakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. If you'd look at -- the name seems to be written again on the left-hand side on the --

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the same?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could turn to the second page, please, and please highlight the second or third paragraph from the bottom. If you'd just scroll down. There's a name which is handwritten in. It says: "Namikom Dankovic."

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Dzankovic. The chief, Mr. Zebic, wrote that in later after he found out the last name. He -- he put it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I move for that to be received into evidence. It has an MFI number at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe it has already -- has already been admitted into the evidence. Right? Yes, it's admitted into evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the next document, MFI D221.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for this previous document, I believe the parties have to work together to sort out the problem of the translation, because we found two versions which are slightly different. Maybe after this sitting the parties could meet together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We most certainly will do that. I said "MFI221." I actually meant P215. I apologise for that. Now, could you just scroll down through that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Salihamidzic, I know that's not particularly -- can you read that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The top, I can. But the bottom part, it's difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please turn the page over, to see whether you can read that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you read that on the screen, or do you need a paper copy -- a paper copy to be given to you?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to read, but I can see that this is some kind of report along the military lines. I didn't write this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you seen this document before coming to give your evidence in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What is your -- can you read the part that says: "The whole of the Jablanica SVK IKM, civilian authorities, and the MUP organs are aware of the incident. Work on the clarification of this case, gathering of operative information on the exact number of dead, how they were murdered, and detection of possible perpetrators has been done in cooperation with (illegible). On-site is currently impossible to carry out because of the large number -- large number of units in the Grabovica area, the attitude of units led by Ramiz Delalic and fear that giving importance to this incident would result in (illegible, missing text) return of the whole unit to Sarajevo, which would directly endanger the planned action on Mostar." Now, that information refers to your police station.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This mentions my report. My name is mentioned. It says that I was -- I was the one who went down there. From what I can see, Mr. Dzankovic is writing a report to his superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I just want you to comment upon, from your knowledge of your investigations, what you saw and what you heard, the accuracy of the part which I just read out to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I don't mind the -- excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please wait for a minute. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just the witness -- it's not the witness's fault. I don't -- I'm quite happy for the Prosecutor to show the witness that passage and -- and ask the witness for his comments, if needs be, but I don't agree that the Prosecutor is allowed to make a comment, as he did on the transcript, to say, "Now, that information" -- he said this at line -- page 26, Line 21, and without asking a question. He just made the statement: "Now, that information refers to your police station." Now, Your Honours have got that in front of you and it plainly doesn't not refer to his police station at all, so that it was a leading question and it was -- it contained false information. So I don't mind the witness being asked to comment on that passage. And he's perfectly entitled to do so as far as he knows. But it's that passage this he's got to comment on, not the proposition that was put by Mr. Re, particularly when it's not a truthful proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: But the commentary was entirely unnecessary about it being false and untruthful. That was a slip on my part and I apologise. I read Jablanica and MUP in my own mind and saw them as the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may ask the witness to comment on that section.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please comment on the accuracy of that section based upon what you yourself observed.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ask see that this is a report which was probably drafted by Dzankovic, from what I can see at the bottom. He is sending a report to his superior command. A joint commission comprising MUP members is mentioned. This is just a proposal. I don't think that this ever actually reached us. This is a proposal that these things should be done, but this is something that was never actually implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, were you involved in any continuing investigation in Grabovica as to what happened in Grabovica, beyond the information you gathered and put in your report on about the 11th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was any further request, to your knowledge, ever made to the Grabovica -- the Jablanica police station to assist in any further investigation of what happened in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no request ever came, as far as I know. Had it arrived, my chief would have probably told me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the last -- when was the next time after you wrote your report -- your official note about the 11th of September, 1993 -- when was the next time you heard about any investigations in relation to what happened in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about any investigation. Our public security station in Jablanica didn't do anything about this. The next time I heard about this case was in 1998, when I was called, after I retired, to see a crime-fighting inspector, to provide a statement about these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown document MFI235.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, have you seen this document -- had you seen this document before you came to The Hague to give your evidence here?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, there's -- if you look at the third -- or the first line underneath "To the chief of the UB, Mr. Jusuf Jasarevic personally." It says: "The following 30 persons lived in the Grabovica area where the massacre of Croatian civilians took place," and there are 30 names listed. And under this it says: "Of these people, Ivan Pranjic and Stoja Pranjic are still alive." Now, you said that -- I think it was Ivan or Stoja Pranjic gave you a list of 30 people who were in Grabovica. Are those the people on the list that they gave you?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thirty people are on this list here. I took their names down by hand according to Stoja's statement. This is obviously typed out. I gave the list to Mr. Zebic, and I never saw it again. I assume that this is the list that I made. It was probably typed out based on the list that I compiled, which was based on the statement of Stoja Pranjic. I know some people from this list. I cannot recall all of them though.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does the information in this report -- if it could just be scrolled down so the witness could see the bottom two paragraphs -- or three paragraphs. Does that accord with the information you had gathered about what happened in Grabovica as of the 11th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. I agree with what it says here, that "Of the above-named inhabitants, Ivan and Stoja Pranjic are still alive and with whom Adnan Solakovic and some of his men were staying, and they protected them and evacuated them." This is more or less the information that I am aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the last paragraph. It has -- and bearing the mind the date of this is the 29th of September, 1993, the last paragraph says: "It has been agreed that the on-site investigation and exhumation work will be carried out by the crime scene of the MUP and the Jablanica military police in cooperation with other professionals." Is that paragraph, based on your knowledge of what was happening on the 29th of September, 1993, correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The on-site investigation and activities relating to the exhumation were never carried out. This is not true, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did your police station have the ability or the expertise in September 1993 to perform exhumations or do pathology investigations?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, perhaps that question ought to be divided in two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I submit that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, maybe the answer is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, it could be so. But there's two different propositions in the question, so that's why I raise the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what our -- the means that are at our disposal. I know that very well. In Jablanica at the time, I believe that we did not have the means to conduct a proper investigation of this case. We didn't have experts who could perform such an investigation, and we didn't have the equipment that was required.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you have the ability to take fingerprints?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did have a kit for simple investigations, on-scene investigations, and we could take fingerprints, but any kind of expert testing was something that we were not able to do. Even identification based on fingerprints was something that we could not do. The kit that we had was mostly used for break-ins, theft, or some other minor crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the ability to interview witnesses? Could you do that?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not? At that point in time, when we had live witnesses or eyewitnesses, we did interview them. As far as eyewitnesses from the units, we were not in a position to do anything in relation to that. I would just like to repeat here what we said in the beginning, and that was that this was not in the jurisdiction of the Jablanica Public Security Station. It was not in its territorial jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your professional opinion as a -- as a police officer of many years standing, could this case have been solved if properly investigated at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that could never be a justified question to ask, and I object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, it's not a proper question to put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown -- I've just got to show him two photographs. It might take a few minutes to do so, and I'll -- I'll be finished then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In less than ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Less than ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We could continue until you finish this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We'll do. Could the witness please be shown photograph P3.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, do you -- do you recognise that, Mr. Salihamidzic, as a photograph of the village of Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You told us you came in from Jablanica. I just want you to draw an arrow where you came from. If you could do it on the right side of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were here and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just put an arrowhead on the -- on the end of that.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said there was a checkpoint. Now, you've drawn a -- a line. Is that the checkpoint you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The line indicates where the checkpoint was, and then in the greenery here you can see the top of the roof of the old railway station building where Ivan Pranjic and his wife, Stoja, lived and where Adnan Solakovic's command was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I just want you to put some numbers on this. Where the checkpoint is, could you put below the checkpoint in the greenery a -- a "1", underneath where the checkpoint was.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps put a -- a line across the bottom of the "1", just to make it a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And then conjoin it.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. And above the arrow pointing to the house, can you please put a "2".

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said there was another checkpoint which you could see in the distance about 100 metres away. Can you please just draw a line where that checkpoint is and maybe put an arrow towards it and a "3".

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The line is indicating the checkpoint; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, there no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P278.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit P9.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, what's that a photograph of, if you can see it there?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness doesn't yet have P9.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What's that a photograph of, Mr. Salihamidzic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph shows where actually Crno Vrelo is, which I mentioned earlier during my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you said you went looking for a body. Does the photo show the area where you were looking for the body?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you put a mark on it with a -- an arrow, just like you did before, where you went to, looking for the body.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you put an arrowhead at the end of where you went to, please. Just to make it completely clear, just an arrowhead at the end of the line.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. And does that show the -- the road on which Celo drove when you were looking for the body, or drove past and stopped?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which way -- I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's upstream from where the checkpoint was. The checkpoint was downstream. When you go upstream, you return towards Jablanica, towards the bridge that joins the left and right bank, and you then continue to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this would be the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's the direction of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just put a "J" on it.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. And in which direction was Celo travelling? Towards Jablanica or towards Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. It's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P279.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That completes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We might have a short break, and we'll resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey. And, Mr. Re used about 100 minutes for his direct examination. I hope you could conduct your cross-examination more or less in the same time frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salihamidzic.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think we -- we'll go straight to the -- the incidents. When you attended at -- at Grabovica on the 9th of September, can you just explain what vehicle you were in.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went there in an official vehicle that belonged to our police station. I think it was a Volkswagen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And can you tell the Tribunal, was it a marked vehicle identified with police markings?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And when you got to the checkpoint, whereabouts did you park that vehicle? On the river side of the road or on the uphill side of the road?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the place where the checkpoint is located, there is a sort of enlargement, an enlarged area. We parked to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. I take it that you took no steps at that point to conceal the fact that you were police attending at Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it was only once you -- well, I withdraw that. I'll come to that question in a minute. All right. Now, you've indicated that you held discussions there with -- with Mr. Solakovic and the two Pranjics. Did you also have the opportunity to speak to Zulfo, the refugee?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I spoke to Mr. Adnan Solakovic and the refugee called Zulfo the most, and I only briefly saw Ivan Pranjic and Stoja. And on that occasion, I don't think it was possible to speak to them, because they were very frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I think you -- yes, I think you indicated that you were able to take a statement from them the following day, when they calmed down a bit. But at the time you saw them in Grabovica, they were terrified; is that right?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, when you turned around to leave the village, you didn't take those two with you because you were concerned that you might endanger yourselves and them by doing that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, as you left the village, you indicated that you stopped at the iron bridge and had a look down on the river-bank to see if you could see a body. And what I wanted to ask you was: Apart from the body that you searched for, did you notice any blood or human remains of any sort on the iron bridge at the time of day that you were there?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bridge by which we stopped -- well, it was an iron bridge, and you are probably referring to the bridge where there were allegedly traces of blood, and that's not the same bridge. That bridge crosses the Neretva; whereas, there's this other one, and on that bridge that crosses the Neretva, there weren't any traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. I'll just have to clarify that, because we've had evidence from other witnesses on this topic. My questions at the moment, first of all, concern the iron bridge, near to which you stopped and -- and performed a search for a body. On that particular iron bridge, is it accurate that you saw no blood or human remains? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. But you have indicated that there's another bridge that may be of interest in this regard. And I want to ask you this question: Did you personally notice any blood on this other bridge?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't stop on that bridge and from the car we didn't see any blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You heard some news about blood on that bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When was it that you heard that news? Was it this day, the 9th of September, or was it the following day, the 10th of September, or was it later on again?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The information that concerned those traces was information that we heard on the following day. When I spoke to Stoja, she told me that the refugees who had gone to get bread that morning noticed blood on the bridge but there were no bodies there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And can you just explain where that bridge is that we're talking about now where -- on which the refugees had reported seeing blood. Is it a bridge -- taking as your reference point the -- the road that goes off to the right bank, departing from the main road. So I'm taking as the reference point the junction of the -- the right bank road with the main M17 highway. Okay? Now, where is the bridge in relation to that junction? Is it back towards Jablanica, or is it further on down towards Mostar?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the bridge is upstream from the junction where the M17 road is. It's about 200 metres in the direction of the power plant dam. When you come down from the main road, then the road goes back towards the dam. You cross the bridge, and then you continue downstream towards the -- the ramp we have mentioned. From the M17 road, you go upstream to the bridge that crosses the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. So it's -- from the road junction we're talking about, it's in the Jablanica direction, rather than the Mostar direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, this bridge that we're now talking about is not the Aleksin Han bridge but a separate bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the Aleksin Han bridge. From Aleksin Han to this bridge, the distance is about almost 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And as far as the jurisdiction of the Jablanica police station goes, in peacetime and in normal circumstances that jurisdiction stopped at the Aleksin Han bridge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you know, there was no change made to that jurisdiction, even after the war started. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So in a -- in a formal sense, the civilian police centre that was supposed to be responsible for Grabovica and the villages south of that, including Dreznica, was the public security centre at Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, there was a police -- or there was a -- sorry, a state security official named Sead Brankovic who was at that time from the Mostar office, even though he was based at -- at your Jablanica police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Now, persisting with the -- with what happened on the 9th. You've already answered many of the questions that I had to the learned Prosecutor, so I'm going to move fairly swiftly through this part of the -- the day. On your way -- after you'd -- after you'd been down to look at the -- at the river, you saw a vehicle, and Mr. Kurt then described a conversation that he had. Can I just ask you: When you saw that vehicle, was it stopped or was it moving?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that the vehicle was leaving. When I came from down below, I could see that the vehicle was crossing the iron bridge and it was heading in the direction of Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And were you able to tell, given the view you had, whether there was one or more than one person in that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't even see who was in the vehicle, nor could I see how many people there were in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, in fact -- well, I understand that. You -- you were told certain things by Mr. Kurt, and then you and he got in the car and drove back to Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, on the way back to Jablanica, did you pass by the checkpoint or a -- a checkpoint, a long-standing checkpoint, actually, at the Aleksin Han bridge?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the Aleksin Han bridge, at the border between the municipality of Jablanica and Mostar, there was a permanent checkpoint manned by policemen from the Jablanica police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was that checkpoint manned in cooperation with the army, or was it wholly and solely a police checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, this checkpoint was manned by the police alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, at some stage in that journey, did you and Mr. Kurt pass by three relatively old people walking on foot in the direction of Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the road from Grabovica to Jablanica, there are two short tunnels. Between the two tunnels, we met two women and a man. One of the women raised her hand. In fact, she stopped the vehicle I was in. I stopped and the woman then told me that they were inhabitants from the left bank of Grabovica. She said they were Croats and they were taking a man away who had survived a serious heart attack a month ago. And given his condition, the temperature, they doubted he would reach Jablanica alive, and they asked me to drive him to Jablanica, which is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And did you get -- did you get the names of those three individuals at the time or not?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know them. And when they got into the car, they told me who they were, that they were the relatives of the wife of one of my friends, Ljubas Stipe, someone I had known from before, his wife. They called her Mica. I don't know if that's her name or nickname. But they told me that they were relatives of theirs. And I took them to Jablanica to his house -- to the flat in which Ljubas Stipe lives, but he worked as an electrical technician in the hydroelectric power plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. And once -- I asked you whether you got their names. Do you -- did you in subsequent times learn the names of these people?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really didn't ask about their names. It wasn't necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, that's okay. All right. So that your first thing -- the first thing you did when you got back to Jablanica was to take -- take those civilians to their relative's house. When you went back to the police station, did you have Mr. Kurt with you at that time, or -- or did you drop him off somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he left before, and I went to the station on my own and briefed Mr. Zebic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. Can you just explain where you took Mr. Kurt to before you -- before you went back to the police station.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think he got out at the administrative building of the Granit facility, which is where part of the command of the 44th Brigade was located at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask you, although I'm getting the narrative at the moment, I'll just pause there. Did you know a 44th Brigade security officer, SVB officer, named Zajko Sihirlic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him. I had known him in peacetime. He also worked in the Jablanica power plant, and he still works there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Just in -- in terms of the building where you dropped off Mr. Kurt. Was that also the building where Mr. Sihirlic worked at that time?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't answer that question. I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. And after that, you -- you made a -- you went to the police station and gave a briefing to your senior -- to your chief, Emin Zebic. After that time, did you make contact with Nehru Manjusak, with a view to rescuing the -- the two elderly people that you'd seen in the old railway station at Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Were you able to do that by telephone, given the telephone situation in Jablanica at the time, or did you have to use some other form of communication?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I went there personally. I went to the house in which Olga Krstic lives together with her son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand and can you -- you don't have to be precise about this, but just to give an estimate: Approximately how long were you away from the police station undertaking that task?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I was away for more than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand and after that, you formed the opinion that before any other steps were taken, it was best to give Mr. Manjusak and, indeed, Zuka some time to accomplish the task of rescuing these two persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told Nehru Manjusak that he should do that as soon as possible, and I think that he listened to my advice and that he left quite soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I just wanted to clarify what your position was about the steps that you were going to take or might -- might take after that time. Did you form the opinion that it was best to allow him a short period of time at least to get to Grabovica and get out again before anything else happened?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Adnan Solakovic had warned me. He said that he couldn't guarantee for the lives of those two elderly Croats who were in that house and I believed that this should be done as a matter of priority and that is why I proceeded in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I -- I understand that completely. Well, my question is, then: Did you become aware that Mr. Manjusak and Zuka had successfully completed that mission?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that that evening. On the following day, in the morning, I went to see whether Stoja and Ivan had been taken out. And when I saw that that had been done, I was happy. And then the circumstances were more normal to have a discussion about this affair.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I understand that. Now, after you had made that arrangement, did you go back to the -- to the police station and speak once again to Mr. Zebic?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned to the police station, and afterwards Mr. Emin Zebic summoned me. I was in my office. He called me because at the time Zuka and Edib Saric had come to see him. He asked me to come to see him, to see what they were discussing, and to exchange our opinions on what had happened. And I was present when Zuka said that there had been a review.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Now, I just want to be clear about -- about when this particular meeting took place in the offices of -- of Mr. Zebic. You've indicated that you -- I just want to make sure I'm right. So you correct me if this order of events is wrong. Okay? Firstly, you came back from Grabovica and you took the -- the three travellers to their relative's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Next you dropped off Mr. Kurt where he had to go, at the 44th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Next you went back to see Mr. Zebic at the police station.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, we're on the 9th. Definitely we're still on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the 9th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: AHMED SALIHAMIDZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
